content.text: Symbiotic Being, a Dark Gift feat, gives you a powerful boost to saving throws at the cost of a second personality occasionally highjacking your character. Sustained Symbiosis and an incredibly powerful defense for any character, and the skill proficiency is great, making this a powerful feat for any character that can deal with the drawbacks of the symbiote.

The symbiote is a unique mechanic. The DM has a huge amount of freedom to decide the symbiote’s goals and how that manifests. If you’re considering this feat, have a long, detailed conversation with your DM about how you both want to handle things.

Because the natural 1 mechanic calls for a Charisma save, the ideal character for this feat has high hit dice and also good Charisma, which limits your options to Paladins and a handful of other martial builds. But don’t let that limit you: Sustained Symbiosis is great regardless of hit die size, so anyone with proficiency in Charisma saves will find a lot of value here.
No mechanical effect other than clarifying that you get to keep the feat even if you die.
Proficiency in one skill and one language. The list of skill options includes more than half of the skills in the game.

An excellent boost to your saving throws. Snce you’re rolling a hit die, it’s more impactful if you have bigger hit dice, making this great for Barbarians but less impactful for Wizards. But even with a small hit die, adding a d6 to a failed saving throw can have a huge impact.
Of all of the Dark Gifts, this is the hardest drawback to predict because it’s so subjective.

sections.heading: How Does the Natural 1 Mechanic Work For Dark Gift Feats?

content.text: It’s not totally clear how the natural 1 mechanic interacts with reroll mechanics like the Halfling’s Lucky feature or with Advantage/Disadvantage. Dark Gifts’ drawbacks trigger “Immediately after you make a D20 Test and roll a 1 on the d20.” How your DM interprets this text can make Dark Gifts dramatically more or less risky.

The intent may be that you only care about the final d20 result. If you roll with Advantage and get a natural 1 on one die, you only care about the d20 that you keep. If this is the case, you can protect yourself with the Halfling’s Lucky feature or by using Heroic Inspiration to reroll. Of course, that makes Dark Gift feats only threatening if you don’t have Heroic Inspiration to rescue you.

If the intent is instead that you trigger the effect if you roll a natural 1 on any d20 rolled during the test, rerolls, Advantage, and Disadvantage all become terrifying risks because they now increase your odds of triggering the save. And can you be forced to save multiple times on one D20 Test?
I think the intent is that you look at the final result after rerolls, etc., because the game treats you as having rolled that number. But check with your DM about how they plan to interpet the text.
